summary: Shechen Gyaltsab (1871–1926) was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Dilgo Khyentse and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Shechen Rabjam Rinpoche (born 1966) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under spiritual teacher Dilgo Khyentse and founded Karuna-Shechen in 2000.

Sheila Jasanoff (born 1944) studied at Radcliffe College, the University of Bonn, Harvard University, and Harvard Law School. She held academic posts at Cornell University (circa 1978–1998) and Harvard University, serving as a professor from circa 1998.

Shek-wing Tam (1935–2024) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Dudjom Rinpoche, Yingguang Qu, and Yui Chi Lau. He founded the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies Association in North America and served as a professor at Renmin University.

Sheldon Pollock (born 1948) is an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held professorships at the University of Iowa, the University of Chicago, and Columbia University (circa 2005–2022).

Sheng Yen (1931–2009) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Jing'an Temple Buddhist Academy and Rissho University. He taught at National Cheng Kung University and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies, and founded Dharma Drum Mountain in 1989.

Shenghai Li works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he was supervised by Donald R. Davis Jr. and studied with Charles Hallisey and Gudrun Bühnemann, among other teachers.

Shenpen Hookham (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. She studied at the University of Reading and completed a D.Phil at the University of Oxford under Michael M. Broido, while also studying under Kalu Rinpoche and other teachers.
Zhenphen Chökyi Nangwa (1871–1927) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Patrul Rinpoche around 1885–1887 and held a post at Dzogchen Monastery.

Sherab Gyatso (1884–1968) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Labrang and Drepung Monasteries. He founded the Buddhist Association of China, serving as president (circa 1953–1966), and was Dean at the Buddhist Academy of China.

Sherry B. Ortner (born 1941) is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD from the University of Chicago. She held posts at Sarah Lawrence College, the University of Michigan (circa 1977–1994), and UCLA.
Sherry Chayat (born 1943) works in religious and Buddhist studies. She studied at Vassar College and trained under Eido Tai Shimano from circa 1974 to 1998, whom she succeeded in 2011.

Shichang Ma (1934–2018) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He worked as a researcher at Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and joined the Archaeology Department at Peking University in 1982.

Shigeki Kaizuka (1904–1987) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1925 to 1928 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1937 to 1968.

Shigeki Kudo (born 1931) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Kyoto University as an assistant, Shuchiin University as an assistant professor, and International Buddhist University as an assistant professor (attested 1972–1973).

Shigeki Moro (born 1972) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He studied at Waseda, Toyo, and Kansai universities. He served as an associate professor at Hanazono University (2002–2015) and became a professor at Waseda University in 2025.
Shigemasa Fukui (born 1935) is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University from circa 1954 to 1958 and later served as a professor there from circa 1978 to 2006.

Shigemitsu Dando (1913–2012) studied at the University of Tokyo under Seiichiro Ono (circa 1932–1935). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1937–1974), Keio University, and the Supreme Court of Japan (circa 1974–1983).

Shigeo Kamata (1927–2001) studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, he served as a professor at the University of Tokyo, Aichi Gakuin University, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Shigeo Yokoyama (born 1954) is a scholar of religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1973 to 1984 and later held academic posts at Okayama University (circa 1988–1994) and Nara Women's University (circa 1994–2019).
